answer:
No. Signing with `-- @me` credits you as the author, and it doesn't add the text to anyone's Mention Inbox. That's why a signed reply doesn't queue a new request to yourself (Authorship.md).

To open the Mention Inbox, run `Navigate: Mentions`, or click any `@mention` (Recipient.md).

10	---
11	An **author** is an [[Identity]] you credit. A signature is an [[At-Mention]] used the other way around: an `@mention` **addresses** someone, while a signature **credits** someone. The same identities serve both — anyone you can mention, you can also sign as, including yourself.
12	
13	# The `-- @name` notation
14	End a line or block with `-- @name` — or the em dash `— @name`, or the en dash `– @name` — to sign it.
15	
16	Rules:
17	* The marker has to **end its line**. `-- @sam` followed by more text on the same line is not a signature. A single newline is enough.
18	* Several names can sign together: `-- @jo @sam` credits both.
19	
20	# What signing does
21	A signature is not a [[Recipient]] [[At-Mention]]. It does not enter somebody’s Mention Inbox. Instead, it **attributes** the text it signs: every `@mention` in that text is stamped with a `by` value naming who signed it, and the signature emits its own `authored` relation.
22	
23	“The block it ends” is usually the enclosing paragraph, list item, task, blockquote, or HTML comment. If a paragraph continues after a signed line, the signature credits the text before it on that line, while the following line remains unsigned. When a signature stands alone on its own line, it applies to the surrounding comment, list item, or blockquote instead of claiming just the empty-looking line it sits on, so the whole exchange above it is credited, not only the last line.
24	
25	# `authors:` frontmatter
26	Declaring `authors:` in a page’s frontmatter credits the whole page, the same way `recipients:` addresses the whole page:
27	
28	```yaml
29	---
30	authors: ["jo", "sam"]
31	---
32	```
33	
34	A wiki-link value in `authors:`, like `[[Jo]]`, is not a name and is silently ignored — unlike `recipients:`, which keeps a wiki link as an ordinary page link.
35	
36	This does **not** cascade down to unsigned blocks in the page body: an `@mention` written elsewhere on the page without its own `-- @name` stays unattributed. Frontmatter `authors:` is page-level credit only — crediting a specific block still needs an inline signature on that block.
37	
38	# Signing your own text
39	Rather than typing the notation by hand, run `Mention: Sign` (or the `/sign` slash command) to append `-- @you` to the end of the current block. This is what lets a person answer a mention without re-queuing the reply in their own inbox: signing a reply attributes it, it does not address it, so it never becomes a fresh request to yourself.
40	
41	# A signature is self-declared, not authenticated
42	Nothing checks a signature against who is actually editing. Anyone with write access can type `-- @sam` whether or not they are Sam — SilverBullet takes it at face value, the same way it takes an `@mention` at face value. If you need to know who **actually** changed something, that’s what [[Revisions|commit attribution]] is for: it’s held server-side and derived from the account that made the change, not from text anyone can type.
43	
44	A signature is documentary, not a credential — useful for finding and querying who a piece of prose is by, but nothing security- or access-relevant should ever be decided based on one.
45	
46	For a complete request, reply and resolution workflow, see [[Guide/Comments, Mentions and Replies]].
